text:
Mika: Quick sync — proposing a canonical eval for the new "decoder-skim" speculative variant on llamaX-70b-4bit. Goal: measure latency/throughput uplift and quality regressions vs baseline (greedy). Protocol below, plz review. TL;DR: 3 seeds, 1k prompts, prompt distro 40/40/20 short/medium/long; temps 0.0 and 0.2; pairwise A/B on 500 samples for human-like quality.

AJ: Quick Q — do we include KV-warmup in p50/p95? that significantly changes tails.

Mika: Yes — measure both cold (no KV) and warm (single prefix run) scenarios. We should report both. Cold = fresh model start, Warm = 1 full convo warmup for each prompt length bucket.

Sam: Add note: run 3 different batching configs (batch=1 continuous, batch=8 latency-optimized, batch=32 throughput) so we can see how speculative interacts with batching.

Natalie: For quality, let's do automated pass (BLEU, ROUGE, PPL) + pairwise human preference on 500 samples stratified by prompt length and task type (qa, summarization, code). Use blind labeling and pair each speculative output vs baseline. Threshold: if human win-rate < 0.95 * baseline win-rate we treat as regression candidate.

Ravi: Dataset source? use: 300 code prompts from internal codebench, 400 qa from NQ + in-house hard-qa, 300 summarization from long-doc testset. Shuffle fixed seed per run.

Mika: Agree. Also record token-level divergence rate (fraction of tokens where speculative path picks a different token than baseline greedy). Capture top-k diff histogram.

bench-bot: Suggested bench harness command:
```\n./run_harness --model llamaX-70b-4bit --exp decoder-skim --seeds 3 \
  --prompts /datasets/decoder_skim_prompts.jsonl --batch-configs "1,8,32" \
  --temps "0.0,0.2" --measure "latency,throughput,ppl,divergence" \
  --kv-warmup "cold,warm"\n```

Mika: Good. Add infra note: pin to same kernel/kcomp so perf delta is due to decode logic not kernel changes. Also capture perf counters (SM utilization, memory BW) if available.

AJ: For rollback policy: propose automatic block for rollout if any of: (1) human win-rate drop >= 5% absolute, (2) automated metric delta PPL worse by > 1.0 on summary set, (3) token-divergence > 12% for short prompts. Otherwise allow canary to proceed to 10% traffic. Thoughts?

Natalie: +1 but make exception: if throughput uplift > 2x and latency p50 improves > 20% we can tolerate slightly higher divergence but we must annotate risky cases and run extra pairwise labeling.

Sam: Ops-wise, we'll run canary in staging then prod canary behind canary-splitter with fast rollback hook. ops-bot can schedule canary run for tomorrow @ 03:00 UTC.

ops-bot: Canary scheduled: decoder-skim -> staging at 2026-03-21T03:00:00Z. Deploy link: https://console.redwood.example/deploys/dec-skim-20260321. @oncall notified. :white_check_mark:

Ravi: One more: include a synthetic adversarial prompt set to stress hallucination and safety regressions. If hallucination rate increases by > 1.5x, block.

Mika: Updated eval YAML (single-file canonical config):
```yaml
experiment_name: decoder-skim-canonical
model: llamaX-70b-4bit
seeds: [42, 99, 123]
prompts: /datasets/decoder_skim_prompts.jsonl
prompt_buckets: {short: 400, medium: 400, long: 200}
batch_configs: [1, 8, 32]
temperatures: [0.0, 0.2]
kv_warmup: [cold, warm]
metrics:
  - latency: [p50, p95, p99]
  - throughput: tokens/sec
  - quality: [ppl, rouge, bleu]
  - human_pairwise: 500
  - divergence: token_diff_rate
  - safety: hallucination_rate
rollback_rules:
  - human_winrate_drop_abs >= 0.05 -> block
  - ppl_delta >= 1.0 -> block
  - divergence_short >= 0.12 -> hold
  - hallucination_multiplier >= 1.5 -> block
reporting: /reports/decoder_skim/{{timestamp}}.csv
```

Natalie: Looks good. Add: labeler instructions -> blind A/B, randomize left/right, show full context, ask: "Which answer would you prefer in product, or no preference?" (options: A/B/no-pref). Capture time-per-label too.

Mika: I'll run the harness tomorrow with bench-bot, collect automated metrics, then kick off pairwise labeling for any cases where automatic signals indicate potential regressions. Will post results here. Thanks all. :rocket:
